source.cantonalMultiplierLaw: https://www.estv2.admin.ch/stp/kb/ne-fr.pdf (Feuille cantonale Neuchâtel; cites Art. premier al. 6 DCICdirPP: 124% pour 2025 et 2026)
source.bfsMunicipalityList: internal register data/raw/bfs_municipalities_register.csv (already present in this project, filtered to cantonCode=NE)

notes: YEAR: 2026. The cantonal coefficient (124%) is legally fixed for both 2025 AND 2026 by Art. premier al. 6 of the Décret fixant les coefficients annuels (DCICdirPP), confirmed verbatim in the ESTV Feuille cantonale Neuchâtel ('Pour l'année 2025 et 2026, le coefficient de l'impôt cantonal direct dû par les personnes physiques est fixé à 124% de l'impôt de base'). The barème (bracket) tables used are the canton's own 'Barème de référence' explicitly valid for fiscal periods 2024 to 2026 (unchanged since 2024; a NEW barème with a different 55%->52%-style splitting adjustment does not recur until fiscal period 2027, per the source page's own '2023 et dès 2027' vs '2024 à 2026' document split), so 2026 uses the same reference barème as 2024-2025 — this is confirmed current and enacted, not a placeholder. MECHANISM (fundamentally different from most other cantons, similar in SPIRIT to Valais): Neuchâtel does NOT publish a simple discrete marginal-bracket law table. Instead Art. 40 LCdir (Loi sur les contributions directes) defines income tax via a continuous AVERAGE-RATE ('taux') formula, and the canton publishes a giant official lookup table ('Barème de référence', impôt de base = coefficient 1.00 = 100%) giving, for every CHF 100 of taxable income from CHF 0 up to CHF 1'000'000+, the exact average rate and resulting tax. The underlying legal formula itself was not needed for this dataset because the canton's own pre-computed table was used directly. THE BREAKPOINT TABLES ABOVE are a piecewise-linear approximation of the true (continuously-varying) MARGINAL rate, derived by numerically differentiating the official table (finite differences over a 500 CHF sliding window at 100 CHF sampling resolution, then run-length-merging consecutive samples whose marginal rate agreed within a 0.0012 tolerance) — NOT an official table in its own right. Verification: reconstructing cumulative tax from these breakpoints reproduces the source table to within about 0.02%-0.3% at spot-checked income levels (e.g. official single tax at CHF 1'000'000 = CHF 136'548.80 vs this table's reconstruction = CHF 136'574.09, a CHF 25.29 / 0.02% difference; at CHF 100'000, official CHF 10'875.90 vs reconstructed CHF 10'900.27, a 0.22% difference) — small but non-zero errors are an expected, documented consequence of approximating a smoothly-curving average-rate function with straight marginal segments; a developer needing exact-to-the-rappen output should use the official per-CHF100 lookup table (SCCO_bareme_revenu_PP_2024.pdf, valid 2024-2026) directly instead of this breakpoint approximation. QUIRK (genuine, verified, not a sampling artifact): the marginal rate for singles is NON-monotonic, rising smoothly from ~2% (CHF 7'800) up to a local peak of ~16.0% around CHF 185'500-205'500, then DROPPING sharply to 13.37% at CHF 206'000 and staying there through CHF 300'000, before rising again in two further flat steps (13.61% from CHF 308'800, 13.86% from CHF 411'800 onward, essentially flat/asymptotic beyond that — verified constant to 4 decimal places out to CHF 1'000'000 in the source table). This 'hump-then-drop-then-reflatten' shape is a real, confirmed feature of NE's rate design (directly visible in, and reconstructed from, the official table's own Taux column), analogous to (but differently shaped from) Valais's similar continuous-rate hump — flag this prominently to any developer who assumes marginal rates only increase with income. MARRIED/SPLITTING MECHANISM (NOT a divisor, NOT the AG/SO-style 'scale the tax by dividing income and remultiplying' pattern): per Art. 40 LCdir and the canton's own explanation, for married couples living in a common household and single parents with dependent children, the RATE (only) is looked up using 52% of the couple's combined taxable income/wealth (not 50%, not the full amount) — i.e. Taux_married(X) = Taux_single(0.52*X) — but the resulting rate is then applied to the FULL (unsplit) amount X, giving the closed-form relationship Tax_married(X) = Tax_single(0.52*X) / 0.52. This was verified by direct comparison against the official married column of the source table at 9 sampled points from CHF 7'800 to CHF 907'800 (agreement to 4 significant figures throughout, e.g. at X=207'800: official married average rate 11.1478% vs formula-predicted rate_single(0.52*207'800=108'056) = 11.1510%). Because of this exact relationship, the MARGINAL rate for married filers at income X equals the single marginal rate evaluated at 0.52X — so the married breakpoint table above was derived (not independently re-differentiated, which proved too numerically noisy at low incomes because the underlying average-rate*income formula amplifies the source table's 0.05 CHF rounding into large marginal-rate noise there) by taking every single-table threshold and dividing by 0.52 (multiplying by 1/0.52 ≈ 1.923077), keeping the same rate at each corresponding breakpoint. This was cross-checked against the official married table's own rate-transition points at three widely-spaced verification thresholds (CHF 384'615, 673'077, 961'538, predicted from the single table's CHF 200'000/350'000/500'000 wealth-tax-style transition points) and the transitions were confirmed to occur within the same CHF 1'000 sampling window in the source married column each time. The first nonzero married bracket (CHF 15'000, i.e. approximately CHF 7'700/0.52 ≈ 14'808 rounded up to the next CHF 1'000 table row where displayed tax first rounds to a nonzero cent value) matches the source table's own first nonzero married row. WEALTH TAX: uses the exact same average-rate mechanism and the exact same 52%-of-fortune splitting relationship for married filers (confirmed in the source: 'Le splitting correspond au 52% du revenu ET DE LA FORTUNE'), but unlike income tax, the wealth-tax average-rate table turned out to be an EXACT discrete step function (no continuous curve at all): differentiating the official table showed the marginal rate is perfectly flat within each of 4 bands with sharp, clean transitions, confirmed to 5 decimal places at the exact CHF 1'000 rows straddling each transition (200'000/201'000, 350'000/351'000, 500'000/501'000 for singles). NOTE ON THE ZERO-WEALTH THRESHOLD: the source PDF's own header states the wealth-tax-exempt band is '0 à CHF 50'900', but reconstructing the table's own tax values (e.g. CHF 100'000 -> CHF 150.00; CHF 51'000 -> CHF 3.00) is exactly consistent ONLY with an underlying threshold of CHF 50'000 flat (i.e. Tax(X) = (X-50'000)*0.003 for 50'000<=X<200'000) — this exactly matches the canton's own general public description elsewhere ('la fortune ... est taxée dès 50 000 CHF de fortune nette'). This dataset therefore uses CHF 50'000 as the true threshold and treats the PDF's '50'900' header text as a likely transcription/rounding artifact in that specific document, not as the operative legal threshold — flagged here in case a developer finds a discrepancy against the raw PDF text. QUIRK (wealth tax, both filing statuses): like the income tax, the wealth-tax marginal rate is explicitly NON-monotonic at the top: 0.3% up to CHF 200'000, 0.4% up to CHF 350'000, 0.5% up to CHF 500'000, then DROPS to a flat 0.36% for all wealth above CHF 500'000 (married: same shape, all thresholds divided by 0.52) — directly analogous to Solothurn's and Valais's top-end rate caps; confirmed exactly via the official table's own values (e.g. singles: CHF 499'000 -> CHF 1'795.00 vs CHF 500'000 -> CHF 1'800.00 [+5.00, i.e. 0.5% marginal] vs CHF 501'000 -> CHF 1'803.60 [+3.60, i.e. the new flat 0.36% marginal]). Rates were given in the source as per-mille (‰: 3‰, 4‰, 5‰, 3.6‰) and converted to decimal fractions per wealthTaxRateUnit (e.g. 3‰ -> 0.003). CANTONAL MULTIPLIER MECHANISM: per Art. 268 LCdir, communes compute their communal tax using the exact same reference barème as the canton, multiplied by their OWN separate communal coefficient; the total bill is (impôt de base) * (coefficient d'Etat + coefficient communal), i.e. state and communal shares are each a separate percentage of the same base tax and then summed (not compounded), the same additive pattern used by AG/SO's Steuerfuss mechanism, just called 'coefficient'/'quotité' here instead of 'Steuerfuss'. CHURCH TAX -- MAJOR STRUCTURAL QUIRK, UNIQUE AMONG MOST CANTONS (shared in spirit only with Geneva): Neuchâtel's 'contribution ecclésiastique' is entirely VOLUNTARY, not a compulsory tax multiplier at all. Per Art. 7-8 of the Concordat/CEE (confirmed directly in the ESTV Feuille cantonale Neuchâtel, section 'Impôts ... dans les paroisses'): 'Les Eglises fixent librement mais conjointement le même taux et les mêmes modalités de la contribution ecclésiastique volontaire de leurs membres' — the three state-recognized churches (Eglise réformée évangélique neuchâteloise EREN, Eglise catholique romaine ECR, Eglise catholique chrétienne ECC) jointly agree on ONE single shared rate (not separate reformed/catholic/christ-catholic rates, and NOT varying by municipality or parish at all), which the cantonal tax administration collects for free alongside the ordinary tax bill and remits to the church the taxpayer declares membership of. The current jointly-agreed rate (per EREN's own published fee schedule) is 11% of the taxpayer's last known impôt cantonal direct (cantonal-tax portion only, i.e. after the 124% coefficient but before communal tax) PLUS a flat CHF 10 'taxe de base de solidarité', for individuals (12% for legal entities/businesses). Because it is voluntary (opt-in by religious self-declaration, and a taxpayer can decline to pay it even if declaring a religion) and NOT baked into the compulsory tax-multiplier system the way AG/SO/other cantons' Kirchensteuer is, this dataset deliberately leaves churchTax.reformed and churchTax.catholic as null and sets variesByMunicipality=false (there genuinely is no per-municipality variation — it is one canton-wide voluntary rate) rather than modeling it as a compulsory multiplier; a developer building a full NE tax calculator should treat church contribution as an optional separate line item (roughly 11% of cantonal tax + CHF 10), not as part of the compulsory income/wealth tax computation. MUNICIPALITIES: NE currently has only 24 communes (down from a historical ~28+ due to ongoing mergers), reflecting the most recent merger — Hauterive, Saint-Blaise, Enges and La Tène merged into the new commune 'Laténa' effective 1 January 2024 (visible directly in the coefficients table, which shows these four former communes as 'Voir sous 79 Laténa' for 2024-2026). The commune list, current (2026) coefficients, and their 3-year history (2024/2025/2026) were extracted directly from the canton's own 'Coefficients communaux et cantonal en vigueur dans les communes neuchâteloises' page (an embedded FAQ/table on ne.ch, not a standalone PDF — the page's underlying JSON-LD FAQPage schema was parsed directly for reliability, and cross-checked against the visibly rendered HTML table, both agreeing exactly). All 24 BFS commune numbers were taken from this project's own existing bfs_municipalities_register.csv (already filtered to cantonCode=NE, 24 rows, already reflecting the Laténa merger), which matched the 24 commune names from the coefficients table exactly with no unresolved names. DISTRICT ASSIGNMENT: NE's 6 districts (Neuchâtel, Boudry, Val-de-Travers, Val-de-Ruz, Le Locle, La Chaux-de-Fonds) are not present as a column in this project's BFS register CSV for NE (district fields were blank), so district names in NE_municipalities.json were assigned from general knowledge of Neuchâtel's administrative geography rather than pulled from a canton dataset column — flagged here since, unlike the BFS numbers and coefficients (which are sourced figures), this one field is inferred and should be spot-checked if precision matters. CHURCH MULTIPLIER FIELDS IN NE_municipalities.json are null for every commune, consistent with the canton-wide voluntary, non-municipal contribution mechanism described above (not missing data).
